questions.explanation: ARROGANT means excessively proud and self-important. Its antonym is HUMBLE (modest, not arrogant). Options B/C/D (Proud, Boastful, Haughty) are all synonyms of arrogant, not antonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: MISER means a person who hoards money and spends as little as possible. Its antonym is SPENDTHRIFT (a person who spends money extravagantly). Options A/C/D (Hoarder, Stingy, Frugal) are synonyms or related words, not antonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: BRAVE means showing courage; not afraid of danger. Its antonym is COWARDLY (lacking courage; fearful). Options A/B/D (Bold, Fearless, Daring) are synonyms of brave.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: ANCIENT means very old; belonging to the distant past. Its antonym is MODERN (relating to the present or recent times). Options A/B/C (Old, Archaic, Antiquated) are synonyms of ancient.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: VERBOSE means using more words than necessary; long-winded. Its antonym is CONCISE (giving information clearly using few words). Options B/C/D (Wordy, Talkative, Lengthy) are synonyms or related to verbose.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: LOQUACIOUS means tending to talk a great deal; very talkative. Its antonym is TACITURN (reserved; saying little; uncommunicative). Options A/C/D (Talkative, Verbose, Garrulous) are synonyms of loquacious.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: BENEVOLENT means well-meaning and kindly. Its antonym is MALEVOLENT (having or showing a wish to do evil to others). The prefix 'bene-' means good; 'male-' means bad. Options A/B/D (Generous, Kindly, Charitable) are synonyms of benevolent.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: EPHEMERAL means lasting for a very short time; transitory. Its antonym is PERMANENT (lasting or intended to last indefinitely). Options A/B/C (Transient, Fleeting, Temporary) are synonyms of ephemeral.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: DEARTH means a scarcity or lack of something. Its antonym is ABUNDANCE (a very large quantity; more than enough). Options B/C/D (Scarcity, Shortage, Paucity) are synonyms of dearth.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: ADULTERATE means to make something impure by adding inferior or harmful substances. Its antonym is PURIFY (to remove contaminants; make pure or clean). Options A/C/D (Contaminate, Dilute, Pollute) are synonyms or related to adulterate.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: ZENITH means the highest point reached (literally, the point in the sky directly above; figuratively, the peak of achievement). Its antonym is NADIR (the lowest point). Options A/B/D (Summit, Peak, Apex) are synonyms of zenith.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: CANDID means truthful and straightforward; open and honest. Its antonym is EVASIVE (tending to avoid commitment or direct answers; not frank). Options A/B/C (Frank, Honest, Sincere) are synonyms of candid.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: EXPAND means to become or make larger or more extensive. Its antonym is CONTRACT (to become smaller; to shrink). Options B/C/D (Extend, Enlarge, Broaden) are synonyms of expand.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: LETHARGY means a lack of energy and enthusiasm; sluggishness. Its antonym is ENERGY (the strength and vitality for sustained activity). Options A/C/D (Laziness, Sluggishness, Inertia) are synonyms of lethargy.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: FRUGAL means sparing or economical with money or resources. Its antonym is EXTRAVAGANT (spending much more than necessary; wasteful). Options A/B/D (Thrifty, Economical, Careful) are synonyms of frugal.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: OSTRACISE means to exclude someone from a group or society. Its antonym is WELCOME (to greet someone warmly; to accept or include). Options A/B/D (Exile, Banish, Exclude) are synonyms of ostracise.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: METICULOUS means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. Its antonym is CARELESS (not giving sufficient attention to avoiding errors or harm). Options A/B/C (Precise, Thorough, Careful) are synonyms of meticulous.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: ALACRITY means brisk and cheerful readiness; eagerness to do something. Its antonym is RELUCTANCE (unwillingness or hesitation to do something). Options B/C/D (Eagerness, Enthusiasm, Willingness) are synonyms of alacrity.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: AMELIORATE means to make something bad or unsatisfactory better. Its antonym is WORSEN (to make or become worse; to aggravate). Options A/C/D (Improve, Better, Enhance) are synonyms of ameliorate.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: GARRULOUS means excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters. Its antonym is RETICENT (not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily; reserved or quiet). Options A/B/D (Talkative, Chatty, Verbose) are synonyms of garrulous.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: AUSTERE means severe or strict in manner; having no comforts or luxuries; plain. Its antonym is LAVISH (very rich, elaborate, or luxurious; giving or providing generously). Options A/B/C (Strict, Simple, Harsh) relate to the severity aspect but are not true antonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: OBSEQUIOUS means excessively compliant or deferential; servilely attentive. Its antonym is DEFIANT (boldly resistant; refusing to obey). Options A/C/D (Fawning, Servile, Submissive) are synonyms of obsequious.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: PRUDENT means acting with care and thought for the future; wise and judicious. Its antonym is RECKLESS (acting without thinking of the consequences; heedless of danger). Options B/C/D (Cautious, Wise, Sensible) are synonyms of prudent.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: APATHY means lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern. Its antonym is ENTHUSIASM (great excitement and interest in a subject or cause). Options A/B/C (Indifference, Lethargy, Laziness) are synonyms of apathy.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: DISPERSE means to go or send in different directions; to scatter. Its antonym is GATHER (to come together; to collect or assemble in one place). Options A/B/D (Scatter, Spread, Distribute) are synonyms of disperse.
questions.subject: English
